questions.stem: During G1 phase, the cell grows and carries out its normal functions. Why is this phase sometimes called the 'first growth phase'?

options.text: Because it is when the cell first starts dividing
Because it is the first time the cell has ever grown
Because it is the first period of growth in the cell cycle, occurring before DNA replication
Because the cell only grows during this phase and not at any other time

questions.explanation: G1 is called the 'first growth phase' because it is the first of two growth phases in interphase. During G1, the cell increases in size and produces proteins before DNA replication occurs in S phase. G2 is the second growth phase.
